feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (the 0.12 m / 0.8 kg baseline) ended all 60 trials off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error 0.061-0.070 m and one line-loss event per run. The limit of max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is fixed at 0.06 m for any body_width up to 0.18 m, so the robot's error must come down. I changed only the drivetrain in this package, so the next race isolates the effect of the Builder's track and mass change. The narrower track gives about 20 percent more yaw per unit of turn command, so I reduced kp and raised kd to compensate. Depending on what the next race shows: if the robot still leaves the track early (off_track before about 20 percent progress) with max_error near 0.06 m, and the line-loss count stays at 1, the limit is likely the sensor lead rather than yaw response. Then move the sensor row forward (y from 0.05 to about 0.065 m) before changing the drivetrain further. If steering_oscillation on the slalom rises clearly above the iteration 0 level of about 0.16 while max_error falls, the body has become too responsive, so restore some mass or track width. If the robot finishes the oval or s-bend but stalls or times out on the slalom, the constraint is speed rather than steering, so change the wheel radius or base_speed before changing the sensors.
requested_changes: If the robot still goes off track before 20 percent progress with max_error near 0.06 m and line_loss_events of 1: move the sensor row forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.065 m, since iteration 0 showed the failure happens early and well before the course ends, which points to lead rather than drivetrain.

If steering_oscillation on the slalom rises above about 0.16 while max_error falls: restore mass to 0.7 kg or wheel_track to 0.11 m, because iteration 0 had oscillation near 0.16 at the wider track and any further narrowing will add yaw gain.

If runs finish or reach high progress but do not complete within 3 s: raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m, because iteration 0 showed no completions at all, so speed is the untested constraint and needs a clear result before any further steering change.
